cards.purpose: a 'Prompt' panel that types its text out over the clip; [m:ss] timestamp tags glow orange, a caret blinks, the box auto-scrolls — for showing an AI-tool/video prompt being written
hero for one tool/model: a glassy app-icon tile with the tool's (muted) logo, its name beneath, and an optional subtitle — the 'this is the tool' beat

subtitle.omit_unless: it states what the tool IS or DOES in words the logo and name do not already carry. Never flow narration about the video itself ('First up in the demo', 'Next tool').

cards.purpose: the viewer sees the decision they will be able to make by the end, resolving on beats
cards.anti_intent: a final verdict (use verdict family instead)

question.example: Which One Ships Clips You Can Post?

winner.note: optional index into options; when absent the card is NEUTRAL and every option resolves to accent (a question card must not pre-answer itself)

cards.note: max_reveal_chars set conservatively from the card CSS (gate backfill 2026-07-31).

cards.purpose: a hero statement holds the frame while the supporting items beneath it (each with a concept icon) are struck out in red one per beat; the title marker word gets the accent sweep on the final beat — enacts these-things-keep-failing / keep-needing-hand-fixing
cards.intent: statement with supporting items struck out per beat
cards.anti_intent: a list the narration endorses (use checklist family — a strike means REJECTED); instructions or descriptions of on-screen actions

marker.note: optional verbatim word inside title that gets the accent sweep

icon.note: key from the card ICONS map (doc, clock, layers, bolt, video, search, chat, gear)

cards.note: max_reveal_chars set conservatively from the card CSS (gate backfill 2026-07-31).

cards.purpose: a single punchy centered statement revealed word-by-word with one keyword phrase highlighted in the accent — a standalone emphasis beat (distinct from running captions)
who this video is for — persona chips landing one per beat
cards.note: max_reveal_chars set conservatively from the card CSS (gate backfill 2026-07-31).

cards.purpose: vertical checklist; each row's box fills and checkmark draws in as it reveals on its beat
cards.side_note: side:true is now backed by an auto-fit (the card shrinks its hero 150->100px, then its item text 40->30px, until title and list both fit the current canvas). MEASURED at 1200x1080 with a 30-char title and 5 items up to 38 chars: everything visible, nothing clipped (2026-08-08). Before the auto-fit this card clipped its heading off the top of the frame and its last item off the bottom at side width, while max_beats/max_reveal_chars — measured at 1920 only — reported it as within capacity. Capacities on a side-capable card must be measured at BOTH widths.

cards.purpose: vertical list of icon-tile + text-pill rows revealing one per beat, accent-outlined with a soft glow; optional keyword highlight per row — for enumerating features/capabilities
horizontal bar chart racing from zero to each product's value
monthly vs yearly plan cards side by side with a savings stamp on the yearly plan
cart summary panel where a coupon code applies and the total counts down
comparison table over a storm/particle background; rows cascade in and the winner column glows
S/A/B/C/F tier list ranking tools with logo pills sliding into each tier row
feature comparison matrix; each row of check/cross/value cells reveals on its beat
two-contender VS panel with stats stacked on each side and a center VS badge
2-3 column pricing plan cards with one plan flagged as recommended
full-price bar that slices off discount chunks one by one down to a final price
scored comparison matrix with a reason column; each factor row reveals on its beat

transparent like/subscribe CTA overlay on a dark glass bar: channel disc, thumbs-up fills accent, a cursor flies in and clicks the Subscribe pill so it flips to Subscribed, then the bell rings and tints
transparent pill overlay pointing viewers to the link in the description
transparent overlay decoding a redacted coupon code with a copy-flash sweep
transparent overlay slamming in a discounted price with a strike-through original and save stamp
transparent lower-third name + subtitle pill sliding in at bottom-left
transparent overlay punching in a big savings amount next to a round seal
spoken score badge: label + animated N/10 pill (optional logo; gold only when winner) at the second the score is said
transparent step-progress pill (Step X of Y) with a progress-dot row for tutorial footage
transparent full-width tip/warning banner sliding in along the bottom or top edge
spoken pros/cons pinned to footage: green-check / rose-cross pill chips tick in one per beat and persist, anchored bottom-left

verdict.note: the card branches on this exact string. It had no enum until 2026-08-07, so consistent-ai-influencer c28 authored "pro" and every positive chip rendered as a red cross for the whole video with nothing erroring.

cards.purpose: two-column pros vs cons; each row reveals on its beat
why the viewer should believe the comparison — the test setup stats counting up
cards.note: max_reveal_chars set conservatively from the card CSS (gate backfill 2026-07-31).

cards.purpose: plain numbered agenda list; each row reveals on its beat
re-shown table-of-contents that dims done/upcoming items and highlights the current section
end-of-video recap; each takeaway ticks in with a check badge on its beat
section divider where a glass card flips up from below and settles with a spring bounce

number.note: optional — omit for an UNNUMBERED section card (title only). Numbered section cards are a SERIES: use numbers only when every major section gets one, 01..0N consecutive (lint W22).

title.note: the card shrinks the hero to fit, but only down to the 120px floor. Past ~26 characters it needs a third line and stops reading as a section plate. "Create Your Base Character" is exactly 26 and is the practical ceiling.

cards.purpose: section divider where a big number counts up then scales down as the title and dots ripple in
section divider with drifting light streaks and particles behind an elastic title pop
numbered table-of-contents list; each row reveals on its beat
title card with drifting aurora blobs and a light bar that wipes logo chips into view — THE cold-open pick for multi-product comparisons (products become the visual hero)
title card with a breathing vignette background; title scales in and uniform tool tiles cascade then gently bob — a strong comparison cold-open (products are the hero, every tile identical size)

the full line-up on screen from frame 0, dimmed; each beat POPS one tool tile (scale + ring + desaturation lift) as the voiceover names it, settling the previous one back down. The roll-call card for a comparison intro, and the beat-driven sibling of title-cinematic-float

name.note: must match one platforms[].name exactly; beats are derived, never authored

cards.intent: A comparison roll-call where the script names each tool in turn, so the graphic follows the voiceover instead of dumping the whole lineup at once.
cards.anti_intent: A lineup the script does not enumerate one by one (use title-cinematic-float), or any set whose items have no logo (this card is a logo-tile card — see R_LOGO_TILES).
cards.note: Built 2026-08-01 from owner fold best-ai-video-generator final-v3:1. Every platform MUST carry a logo slug; the letter fallback exists only so a missing asset does not crash the render.

cards.purpose: comparison cold open: two large logo tiles side by side with the product name beneath each and a VS badge between — the compared products ARE the visual hero

title.omit_unless: it adds framing the product names do not already carry

cards.purpose: title card with kinetic line-by-line text reveal for kicker, title, and subtitle
title card with a storm background and the title popping in with an elastic overshoot
verdict card where the winner slides in and five achievement badges pop in one by one
verdict report card with a glowing letter grade; each sub-grade reveals on its beat
verdict card with confetti and a trophy dropping in before the winner card lifts with a gold pulse. ONE winner per card — a dual verdict gets one card per winner, back to back
big animated stat: count-up hero number + label + context line, transparent overlay for demo footage
section opener for one tool/product: TOOL N OF M progress, huge name, positioning line, category chip

side-by-side verdict winners over a confetti stage, one tool column per beat; scales 2-4 winners (layout derives from count). Use for a multi-winner finale — co-winners (ranked:false, all gold) or a ranked podium (ranked:true → gold/silver/bronze/steel). ONE tool per beat.
use-case verdict: persona → winning tool pairs, one pair per beat
credit/unit economics rows: plan → credits → what that actually buys, one row per beat
numbered step flow: process walkthrough nodes revealing left to right, one step per beat
comparison table that builds one row per beat as each product's numbers are spoken; cells pipe-separated in beat text

text.note: pipe-separated cells; prefix a non-first cell with * to render it as a GOOD (green) pill or ! as a BAD (rose) pill — mark the standout value per column

cards.purpose: canvas beat: a spoken headline sentence plus pill chips ticking in one per beat (lists, consequences, criteria)
one spoken sentence alone on the ambient canvas; words appear as spoken and an accent phrase colorizes with them; used INSTEAD of a talking-head bridge

text.note: a declarative STATEMENT (claim, judgment, consequence) that could stand alone as a pull-quote; the verbatim core clause of a longer sentence. Never instructions or on-screen-action descriptions.

cards.purpose: a labeled vessel fills stepwise; each beat adds a measured pour + label chip
cards.intent: Show a metric or capacity filling up stepwise.
cards.anti_intent: Showing multiple items racing or comparing static values without a total.

cards.purpose: Products race as horizontal bars; each beat advances all bars to given values; a stalled bar visibly judders and stops

productLogos.note: index-aligned with products; every graphic should carry a colour mark, not text alone (owner 2026-07-30)

cards.intent: Compare performance or progress of multiple items racing simultaneously.
cards.anti_intent: Showing a single item filling up or stacking up.

cards.purpose: One huge number rolls to each beat's value; a tick strip accumulates marks underneath
cards.intent: Count or tally a single growing number over time with tick marks.
cards.anti_intent: Showing fractions, percentages, or items racing.

cards.purpose: A node chain with a pulse that travels; each beat lights the named step

title.note: 3 words is variant B's limit (vertical chain, least vertical headroom). Declared capacity must be the TIGHTEST variant's, because resolve.mjs picks the variant after the copy is written (c17 overflowed this way, 2026-07-30).

cards.intent: Show progress through a linear sequence of steps.
cards.anti_intent: Showing branching logic or a growing network graph.

cards.purpose: A vertical short-form clip frame that cycles three ways an auto-generated clip comes back broken; each beat lights one failure
cards.intent: The VO claims automated clipping still leaves work behind, and no footage of a bad clip is on screen.
cards.anti_intent: Praising a tool's output, or any moment where real footage of the actual result is already visible.
cards.note: max_reveal_chars set conservatively from the card CSS (gate backfill 2026-07-31).

cards.purpose: A dimmed grid of items; a spotlight sweeps then locks on focus, others fall to 25% opacity

productLogos.note: index-aligned with items; every graphic should carry a colour mark, not text alone (owner 2026-07-30)

cards.intent: Highlight one specific item out of many alternatives.
cards.anti_intent: Showing sequential progress or comparing two items head-to-head.

cards.purpose: five identical matte-black pedestals under one warm key light, each holding a different glass object at its own colour temperature and engraved with the promise it stands for; the key light walks the row, lifting one plinth and letting the rest fall back, and never settles on a winner

tint.note: hex colour temperature for that object glass + halo

label.note: the promise engraved on that plinth — a CATEGORY the tool competes in, never the tool's name

focus.note: 1-based index of the pedestal to pull focus to; a beat naming a missing pedestal is ignored

cards.intent: The cold open of a comparison whose thesis is that the products are NOT interchangeable: the frame shows five different promises and refuses to pick one.
cards.anti_intent: Any moment with a winner, a ranking, or a claim about ONE product. The placards name the PROMISE each pedestal stands for, never the product — a roll-call of tool names belongs on tool-icon/roster-pop, and putting them here says the same thing twice.
cards.note: Headless by design (hero_shape none) — the placards are per-item labels, not a hero. Built 2026-08-01 after the owner rejected a word-synced hook on best-ai-video-generator final-v3:0 and approved this look from a Gemini prompt preview. REVISED 2026-08-02 once the owner saw it move: the depth-of-field focus pull became a light-based one ("all gets blury") and the empty plinths gained engraved promise labels ("just icons and no info, no actual content"). Both were properties a still preview could not show.

cards.purpose: A horizontal timeline; the playhead jumps to each beat's marker, stamping a label above it
cards.anti_intent: Showing a logical pipeline or stacking architecture.

cards.purpose: A zsh-style window slides in and TYPES command with a blinking caret, then prints output. (This is the "show the real thing" device — the command must be real, never pseudo-code.)
cards.intent: Show a real terminal command being executed.
cards.anti_intent: Explaining concepts with pseudo-code or abstract steps.

cards.purpose: two products share one promise, then the frame splits and each side takes the bet it actually makes: for the sentence shape "A and B both promise X, but one does P and the other does Q"
cards.intent: One spoken sentence sets a shared promise and then divides it into two opposing bets; the split enacts the divergence.
cards.anti_intent: More than two products, no shared promise, or numeric stats (use head-to-head or table-rows).
cards.note: Beat card since 2026-07-31 (owner final-v1:1): sides[2] in on-screen order left,right; each beat reveal.name times that side's verdict to its spoken words, so the card stays dynamic and covers the whole concept. Beats in SPOKEN order.

cards.purpose: full-frame dim scrim behind a centred link lockup with a nudging down-arrow: the high-salience "links in the description" call-out
cards.intent: The VO points the viewer to the description and it must actually land; dimming the footage removes every competing target.
cards.anti_intent: A passing mention of the link mid-demo where dimming the screen would hide something the viewer needs to see.

cards.purpose: full-screen tale-of-the-tape comparison intro: the two brand logo tiles face each other across a center seam up top, and each spoken pain pops in as a compact icon+word panel along the lower third, word-synced. For an intro hook naming 2-3 pains before introducing two tools

icon.note: one of: captions, gauge, grid (card-local icon set)

cards.intent: The board carries the whole intro frame: the matchup lands first, then the named pains build beneath it as they are spoken.
cards.anti_intent: Full-frame graphics-only intro: never place an avatar span over it. Never with more than 3 pains, never for a single-tool video.
cards.note: Owner-commissioned 2026-07-31 (v8 fold, full-screen intro). Replaced intro/tape-board-side after the owner rejected the side-mode intro on the v8 review; layout approved from a generated preview frame with three riders: real logos in the tiles, an icon on every pain panel, pain panels smaller than the app titles. Motion toned down by owner instruction.

cards.purpose: one anchor portrait card holds a face; each beat stamps a duplicate into a new scenario frame carrying the IDENTICAL portrait, differing only in a scenario tint — the card PROVES character consistency instead of asserting it
cards.intent: The VO claims one character survives across different scenarios, and the screen is not already showing that comparison side by side.
cards.anti_intent: A lineup of DIFFERENT people, products or options — the duplicates here are deliberately identical, so difference reads as a bug. Also wrong when footage already shows the same-face comparison.

marker.note: one verbatim word inside title that gets the accent sweep

anchorLabel.note: uppercase label under the source card; defaults to "Anchor"

anchorImage.note: the real anchor portrait for the FIRST frame. Omitted renders a flat vector stand-in, which the owner rejects in a finished video (DESIGN.md, real photos beat vector stand-ins).

tint.note: optional rgba wash that separates the frames. It is NOT what makes them different scenarios — beats[].image is. Auto-softened when the beat carries its own image.

image.note: the SAME character in a DIFFERENT scenario for this frame. The face is the constant, the scenario is the variable — a shared image with a colour tint was rejected by the owner (2026-08-07). Falls back to anchorImage if omitted.
